entities.name: Priscus of Epirus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Priscus of Epirus, a renowned Neoplatonist philosopher and theurgist, played a pivotal role in the Classical era of Greek thought. Born of unknown origin, Priscus was a colleague and friend of the celebrated philosopher Maximus of Ephesus, and even befriended the enigmatic Emperor Julian.

As a key figure within the Neoplatonist movement, Priscus's philosophical and theological ideas were heavily influenced by his interactions with other prominent thinkers of the time. The exact nature of his teachings remains somewhat of a mystery, with much of his work surviving only in fragmentary form.

Despite the scarcity of concrete information regarding Priscus's life, his legacy continues to be felt within the realm of classical philosophy, demonstrating the profound impact that his ideas have had on subsequent generations of thinkers.

Through his association with Emperor Julian, Priscus was able to navigate the complexities of imperial politics, offering his counsel to the emperor on matters of state and philosophy.

This enigmatic figure's significance can be gauged by the enduring influence of his philosophical ideas, which continue to shape our understanding of the nature of reality, the human condition, and the mysteries of the divine.

"The universe is a single, indivisible entity; the soul is an integral part of this totality." — Priscus of Epirus
